 More Than 4 Million Tubes of Toothpaste Recalled Nationwide, FDA Warns 
 More Than 4 Million Tubes of Toothpaste Recalled Nationwide, FDA Warns 
 Here’s how to check if your tube is affected.
 By Jenn Gonick Published: Oct 22, 2026 2:23 PM EDT Save Article Share Article Hispanolistic // Getty Images 2 min read Key Points 
 Toothpaste is being recalled nationwide, according to the U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA).
 The recalled tubes do not meet Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) standards.
 Here’s how to tell if your tube is affected.
 If you have a tube of Brush Buddies, Evo, or ARU toothpaste at home, you may want to take a second look at the label before the next time you go to squeeze some onto your toothbrush . Over 4 million tubes of toothpaste have been recalled nationwide, according to the U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA).
 Per the FDA’s announcement , the voluntary recall was initiated by the manufacturing firm Pritam International Private Limited in September over deviations from Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) , which “ensures the quality of drug products by carefully monitoring drug manufacturers’ compliance with [regulations].”
 On October 19, the FDA gave the recall a Class II designation, which means that using the affected products “may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences.” Here’s everything you need to know about the recall .
 Which products are affected by the recall?
 The recall includes 17 toothpaste products distributed nationwide under the brand names Brush Buddies, Evo, and ARU. Check your bathroom for any of the following tubes:

 More information, including lot numbers and expiration dates for each of the recalled toothpastes, can be found in the FDA’s enforcement report .
 What should you do with a recalled product?
 As of right now, the FDA hasn’t announced any injuries or illnesses associated with the recall or issued specific guidance for consumers. But to be safe, if you have any of the recalled toothpaste in your home, you shouldn’t use it. Instead, throw it away or return it to where you bought it for a refund. If you or someone in your family has already used the recalled toothpaste and has any health concerns, contact a doctor right away.
